clue.text: One dwelt towards the north, given case of Scotch that's very bad

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so these letters are written backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
dwelt means lived

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so take its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters S and H

explanation.surface: A grim tale of a northern dweller whose bottle of whisky is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards the north' turns I LIVED upwards into DEVILI; the case of Scotch, SH, finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish, like something fiendish, is an intensifying adjective meaning wicked or extremely bad.

clue.text: Rodent raised two male animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted up, so the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tom (male cat) and a ram (male sheep)

explanation.surface: Someone bred a pair of male animals.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM and RAM written upwards give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmot is a burrowing ground squirrel, a large member of the rodent family.

clue.text: Paddling in ocean incredibly good

indicators.note: something done incredibly is done in an unbelievable way, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Kayaking out at sea is said to be wonderful fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incredibly' looks like it modifies 'good', but it is the signal to shuffle the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoeing is propelling a light boat through water with a paddle.

clue.text: Primitive fellow's grave

parts.note: ur- is a prefix meaning primitive or original, as in Ur-text
a gent is a fellow; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: The burial place of an early man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' tempts as a noun beside 'Primitive fellow', but it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave matter is serious and pressing, so needing immediate attention.

clue.text: Islander heading for cinema rushed to catch film

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter C

indicators.note: to catch something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: rushed means ran
ET is the Spielberg film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: An islander dashes off to the pictures to see a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The film is Spielberg's alien, known by its two initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of Crete, the largest Greek island.

clue.text: Firms working to provide protective covering

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm; two firms give two of them
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Companies are busy supplying some kind of protective layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is the silky case a larva spins to shield itself while it pupates.

clue.text: Picked up doughnut for some stars

indicators.note: a sound picked up is heard, so the answer sounds like the word given

parts.note: a torus is the geometric name for a doughnut shape

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed a doughnut to share with celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: TORUS, the mathematician's doughnut, is said the same way as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the Bull, is a constellation, a group of stars in the zodiac.

clue.text: Cut treatment for side pain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a suture used to close a wound
second meaning: a sharp cramp in the side, often from running

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a reduced therapy, the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture closing a wound and a sudden ache under the ribs share the same name.

clue.text: Queen dons anorak, European queen that's one of thirteen characters across here

definitions.text: one of thirteen characters across here

indicators.note: the queen dons, or puts on, the anorak, so she ends up wrapped inside it

parts.note: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive geek
R is the abbreviation for Regina, queen
a Lett is a Latvian, a European
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch puts on a geek's anorak, while a European queen is one of many characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Every across answer hides a Greek letter: CRETAN has ETA, TAURUS TAU, SCHISM CHI and so on, thirteen in all. An anorak is British slang for a nerdy enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Each across answer conceals a letter of the Greek alphabet, so the answer names that kind of hidden character.

clue.text: Conservative chap's into S&M, creating division

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: taken as its two letters S and M
a chap's thing is his

explanation.surface: A Tory's taste for sadomasochism splits the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or breach within a group, especially a church.

clue.text: Oh dear! Is ground in country no longer?

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay at something being crushed in some former land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as the earth, but it signals OH DEAR IS shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the name of present-day Zimbabwe until 1980, a state that has since been renamed.

clue.text: Native American's somewhat faddish opinions

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tribesman holds rather trendy views.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are an Indigenous people of northeastern Arizona; the 's reads as 'is'.

clue.text: What disciplinarians read has man involved in threesome with delicacy

indicators.note: one piece is involved in, or wrapped up in, another, so it goes inside

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
he is a man, the male pronoun
tact is delicacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a man in a threesome, handled with discretion.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes into TRIO for THERIO, then TACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To read someone the riot act is an idiom for a stern reprimand, which strict superiors deliver.

clue.text: Some wood covered in fancy polish — it's for expert in 8s, say

indicators.note: the wood is covered in the other letters, so they go around it
fancy as a verb hints at reimagining, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: it, with the 's read as 'is' linking to the definition
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture gets a coat of special varnish, suited to a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: '8s' points to the answer at 8 down, Greek letters, an example of what a student of language might study.
explanation.definitionFit: A philologist studies languages and their history, so the ancient Greek alphabet is a typical field.

clue.text: Oscillations in air currents or foliage around east and west

indicators.note: the foliage sits around the compass points, so they go inside

parts.note: leaves are foliage
E is the compass abbreviation for east
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Either weather wobbles or the greenery of trees blowing across the compass.
explanation.walkthrough: E and W go inside LEAVES after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee waves are standing wave patterns in the atmosphere formed downwind of a mountain range.

clue.text: Rogue peed in vessel for disinfectant

indicators.note: one piece is placed in another

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

indicators.note: a rogue thing goes astray and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scoundrel has relieved himself in a ship, needing a cleaning agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a noun for the culprit, but it is an adjective signalling the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep dip is the insecticidal liquid farmers immerse sheep in to kill parasites.

clue.text: Buckle from jacket of fleece turned up in bedroom

indicators.note: one piece is placed in another

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a bedroom

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up reads the letters from the bottom upwards
a word's jacket is its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters F and E

explanation.surface: A buckle off a fleece jacket was found lying in a bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckle' looks like a noun belonging to the jacket; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To buckle and to deform both mean to bend or warp out of shape under pressure.

clue.text: Energise two classical sextets, faintly disheartened

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six, and two of them give VIVI

indicators.note: with its heart, or middle, removed, the word keeps only its ends

parts.note: outer letters F and Y

explanation.surface: Pep up a pair of half-dozen classics that are flagging and dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical' points to Roman numerals, VI and VI; faintly loses everything but FY.
explanation.definitionFit: To vivify is to bring life or animation to something, enlivening it.

clue.text: Outdid frames art gallery trialled

indicators.note: one word frames another, holding it inside

parts.note: bested means outdid or beat
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A rival outshone the exhibition space in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British art galleries, best known for Tate Modern in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that has been beta-tested has been tried out by real users before release.

clue.text: Getting on and being in harmony but not touching

indicators.note: but not says a part is excluded from the word just named

parts.note: agreeing means being in harmony
re means about, concerning or touching on

explanation.surface: Elderly folk getting along nicely though keeping their distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' here means concerning, which is RE; take it out of AGREEING.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, which is what ageing describes.

clue.text: Fight you heard on street during party

indicators.note: one piece comes during another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud, giving a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you

explanation.surface: A brawl you hear about out in the road at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The party is political, not a social gathering: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust-up is an informal word for a scrap or brawl.

clue.text: Going out with partner once having personal charm

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
it is old slang for sex appeal, personal magnetism

explanation.surface: Dating a former partner who has real charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going out' looks like dating, but it defines the noun for an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is the act of leaving, a departure.

clue.text: Ambassador willing to accept honour for England at Wembley, say?

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so it goes inside

parts.note: HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
game means willing, up for it

explanation.surface: A diplomat happy to be decorated for the national football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley is England's national football stadium, so a match there is played on home turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A home game is a match played at the team's own ground, which Wembley is for England.

clue.text: Nurse only half pens records for medical problem

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the records go inside
only half means keep the first half of the word

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in Britain
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: A nurse writes up only half the records of a patient's condition.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse; half gives SIS, which holds EPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepsis is a dangerous bodily reaction to infection, a serious medical condition.

clue.text: Satisfied about cool ending of Rameau composition

indicators.note: one piece goes about, or around, the others

parts.note: met means satisfied, as in met a demand
in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter U

explanation.surface: Pleased with the cool finish of a piece by the French Baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A minuet is a stately dance in triple time and a piece of music written for it, such as Rameau wrote.

clue.text: I'm not sure about small-scale rebellion

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: um is a hesitant noise meaning I'm not sure
tiny means very small

explanation.surface: Someone doubtful about a minor uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutiny is an open revolt against authority, especially by sailors or soldiers.
